derivedFrom: figure 9.1's five steps and the decisions they cite, as section 9 states them from the 3.4 correction of 2026-09-26, applied outside this repository and without running the level builder. The candidates are the ones the earlier derivation collected from the committed bar files over the last sixty sessions; they are merged where two are closer than half a typical day's move, a chain wider than two typical days' moves is split at its widest gap, one touch is added for each visit over the window's sessions, read at the adjusted prices the store holds, unless the visit holds a session the band has as a swing or a retracement, roles are assigned against the last close with the nearest on each side marked, and the strength is scored. The builder's output was read only after this was written, and the two agreed on every band and every member. A builder merging on the wrong distance would still agree with a band set taken from itself.

window.note: the level window, the same sixty sessions the volume profile accumulates over. Swings are taken from inside it and only where confirmed on or before the as-of date, which is what stops a band resting on a peak nobody could have seen.

close.note: the last session's close, which is what roles are assigned against.

mergeDistance.note: half a typical day's move, being the average true range at the as-of session rounded to the store's four places and halved. Stated per name because it is the number the merge turns on and it differs by name, which is what makes it a distance rather than a threshold. Read against the average true range the store holds at each name's as-of session, at the fraction section 17's row states and the builder merges at. Twice it is the typical move, and four times it is the widest a band may be.

rows.note: every band for every name, in the order the primary key sorts them. A zero width band is a real band: a single candidate with nothing within half a typical day's move of it is a level at one price, which is how the worked example states a resistance at 996 and another at 1057. AAPL's band from 299.7415 to 320.28 and KEYS's from 300.87 to 332.78 were each one chain of close pairs wider than two typical moves, and each is three bands here, split at their widest gaps.

members.note: every member of every band, keyed by the band's low edge, in the order the stored JSON carries them. A touch is a visit rather than a session, so a band the price sat in for weeks holds one touch for the stay, and a visit holding one of the band's own swings or retracements adds none: the swing low of 2026-06-25 at 273.5141 is one member where it was a swing and a touch of the same session.

nearest.note: the nearest support and the nearest resistance the universe read states for each name, which each row's distance is drawn to. Taken from the rows above rather than from a run: the high edge of the name's one marked support band and the low edge of its one marked resistance band, the edge of each that faces the close. MSFT's and NFLX's marked resistance and all four marked supports have width, so the far edge of any of them reads differently from the near one. The split bands leave every one of these edges where it was, because each marked band's facing edge was the end of its chain nearest the close.

workedBand.name: AAPL
workedBand.note: the band holding the five retracements, and the one where each of the three bonuses is worth following. One point per member, touches included, plus one for a member whose evidence occurred in the last twenty sessions, plus one where a retracement and a swing are both anchors, plus one where the band holds a shelf. It holds one touch, the visit from 2026-07-02 to 2026-07-14, because the stay from 2026-07-31 to 2026-09-01 holds 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-20, the sessions of its swing high and of its retracements, so that visit is already in the band.

profileWindow.note: the profile accumulates over the same sixty sessions the level window uses, and this is the first checkpoint where that is observable rather than stated: a band resting on a shelf is a band whose member came from the profile, and the two would disagree if the windows did.

retracementEnds.note: the five retracements are drawn between the window's last swing high and its last swing low, in whichever order they occurred, so all five land together and the set is the one that measures from the end the move finished at.

shelfCreatesABand.note: a band whose only anchor is a volume shelf, which is a band on volume alone. It is the case the ruling exists for: under the other reading, that a shelf only ranks, this band would not exist and the range would be something the report cannot state. One name in this fixture has one, which is why the ruling was assertable at 3.4 rather than waiting for 3.6.
